title: Daily Market Digest
subtitle: Market closed, summarizing Friday, September 11, 2026 session

items.headline: U.S. Stocks Rebound on Easing Oil Prices and Inflation Data; Major Indices End Week Lower
items.summary: Major U.S. stock indices closed sharply higher on Friday, breaking a four-day losing streak, as Brent crude oil prices retreated by nearly 3% and August inflation data largely met economists' expectations. This rebound reinforced market sentiment for an upcoming Federal Reserve interest rate hike. Despite Friday's gains, all major indexes finished the holiday-shortened trading week in negative territory.

items.headline: Lumentum Leads Weekly S&P 500 Gainers on AI Demand
items.summary: Lumentum Holdings ($LITE) was a top S&P 500 performer for the week, returning approximately +9.02%. The optical and photonics technology company benefited from its ties to AI and data center infrastructure requirements.

items.headline: Hewlett Packard Enterprise Surges on AI Optimism
items.summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise ($HPE) saw a weekly gain of approximately +7.15%, with strong performance on Friday driven by renewed investor optimism in the tech sector, particularly around AI.

items.headline: TKO Group Posts Solid Weekly Gains
items.summary: TKO Group Holdings ($TKO) finished the week with a notable return of approximately +5.89%, positioning it among the top S&P 500 performers.

items.headline: CooperCompanies Plunges on Weak Revenue and Outlook
items.summary: CooperCompanies ($COO) was the biggest S&P 500 loser for the week, down about -22.98%. The medical-device company's shares sold off sharply after reporting weaker-than-expected quarterly revenue and reducing its full-year outlook.

items.headline: Casey's General Stores Falls on Disappointing Sales
items.summary: Casey's General Stores ($CASY) ranked among the week's biggest losers, falling approximately -16.46% after its fiscal first-quarter results showed comparable-store sales below expectations.

items.headline: FactSet Drops Amid Market Pressures
items.summary: FactSet ($FDS) experienced a significant weekly decline of approximately -14%, reflecting broader market pressures and company-specific investor adjustments.

items.headline: August Inflation Data Solidifies Expectations for Fed Rate Hike
items.summary: The August Consumer Price Index (CPI) showed a 0.4% month-over-month increase and a 3.4% year-over-year rise, largely meeting headline forecasts. However, core CPI, excluding volatile food and energy, rose 0.3% monthly, slightly exceeding expectations. This data, coupled with elevated oil prices, has led markets to price in an over 85% probability of a 25-basis-point Federal Reserve rate hike at its September 16th meeting.

items.headline: Technology and Communication Services Lead Rally; Utilities and Healthcare Lag
items.summary: On Friday, Communication Services (+1.35%) and Information Technology (+1.60%) emerged as the top-performing sectors, buoyed by a rotation into riskier assets and AI optimism. Conversely, Utilities (-0.34%) and Health Care (-0.11%) were among the lagging sectors, sensitive to rising Treasury yields and shifting market preferences.

items.headline: Kroger Reports Q2, Oracle Exceeds Estimates Boosting Tech Sector
items.summary: Kroger Co. ($KR) reported its second-quarter 2026 results on Friday, reaffirming its full-year adjusted net earnings per diluted share guidance but lowering its identical sales outlook without fuel. Meanwhile, Oracle ($ORCL) announced after Thursday's close that it beat fiscal first-quarter estimates and hiked its profit guidance, contributing to the tech sector's strong performance on Friday.

items.headline: Oil Prices Ease on Friday, Remaining a Key Inflationary Concern
items.summary: Brent crude oil prices saw a nearly 3% drop on Friday, providing some relief to inflation concerns. However, oil prices remained significantly higher for the week amid ongoing geopolitical tensions, particularly the intensifying Iran conflict, which has prompted Saudi Arabia to close energy facilities and disrupted global energy markets.
